messages:
noah: Heads-up — PR #8429 is ready for final review but it's gated on the RFC. I linked the RFC below and flagged the rollout window. Need arch eyes before we merge.

noah: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8429
noah: RFC: https://rfc.redwood.ai/r/2026-kv-prefix-routing (this is the doc we referenced in the code comments) :link:

maria: Thanks — quick Q: does this change require a canary longer than usual?

noah: Short answer: probably. The KV-prefix routing touches cache invalidation logic; canary suggested 48h with traffic ramp from 1% -> 10% -> 25%.

ajay: Can you paste the SLO impact summary here? Ops wants numbers before sign-off.

noah: Sure — rough numbers from local perf tests: p50 token latency +2ms, p95 +18ms under steady load. CPU/GPU throughput unchanged. Risk is cache-miss tail when switching prefixes. We're adding automatic fallback to legacy routing on errors.

lisa: What does fallback look like? Does it change model selection or just routing table?

noah: Fallback reverts to the previous routing table (no model change). It's a stateless switch on a per-request error; we log and increment a metric `kv_routing.fallback_count`.

maria: deploy-bot ran tests, any flakiness in e2e?

deploy-bot: CI results for PR #8429: unit tests ✅, integration tests ✅, canary-smoke ❌ (1 flaky failure: kv-cache TTL check). See pipeline: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/8429

david: Re: flaky TTL check — I can look tomorrow AM. If we can get a retry in the test or tighten timing, should be fine.

ajay: From architecture side I'm especially looking for: migration plan, invariant guarantees, and how we detect/roll back if cache corruption appears. Is that in the RFC?

noah: RFC section 4 covers migration and invariants. Short summary here: rolling config rollout, verification queries, and a healthcheck that stalls traffic to new routing when >0.5% fallback rate for 10m. Rollback is automated via config flag.

lisa: Ok I can do a quick read and give a +1 if the healthcheck thresholds look sane. Ping me when CI is green and the flaky TTL test is addressed. :thumbsup:

maria: @ajay any other arch concerns or do you need more context from the RFC?

ajay: I'll skim the RFC now. If I don't comment by EOD, assume no blocking arch comments but will require an explicit sign-off from eng-arch channel before merge.

noah: Thanks — I'll fix the flaky test and update the RFC with a clearer failure mode flow. Will post back here when done.

maria: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

noah: tagging for follow-up: @lisa @ajay @david — once CI is bright green and you folks OK, I'll schedule the 48h canary and merge window.
